trust_decision.summary: Which network peers may reach the unauthenticated /__marmite__/ write API (content, config, file, init) is decided only by the listening interface chosen in server::start; at the pinned commit the CLI default is 0.0.0.0 and a bind failure silently falls back to 0.0.0.0:0, with no auth, Host or Origin check in handle_request.

landing_point.why: Advisory says the dev server exposes the API unauthenticated; the first thing to check is the --bind default, which is 0.0.0.0:8000.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `--serve` (any --bind, incl. explicit 127.0.0.1) when the requested address fails to bind -> fallback to FALLBACK_BIND_ADDRESS (src/server.rs:26)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/server.rs:26 and src/server.rs:104 (port-conflict fallback hard-coded to 0.0.0.0:0, overriding a loopback --bind)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fallback only triggers on a port conflict/bind error, looks like robustness code, and the user already asked for a specific address, so a solver who just changes the --bind default to 127.0.0.1 will consider the issue closed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Explicit `--bind 0.0.0.0:8000` for LAN sharing must keep working, and an occupied port must still fall back to an OS-assigned port (now on the same interface); an over-broad fix that forces loopback, rejects non-loopback binds, or removes the fallback breaks documented behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: explicit IPv4 loopback with port conflict -> fallback keeps 127.0.0.1
IPv6 [::1] with port conflict -> fallback keeps ::1 (fix.diff:227)
hostname / multi-address resolution via ToSocketAddrs, all ports zeroed (fix.diff:167-175)
invalid address -> error, no fallback to all interfaces (fix.diff:244-246)

O7_producer.where: src/cli.rs:59-61 (clap default supplies the bind address consumed at src/main.rs:95)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Loopback-bound API still accepts any Host/Origin, so browser-mediated requests (cross-site POST / DNS rebinding) reach the same unauthenticated write handlers; the fix adds no Host/Origin or token check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different mechanism (CSRF/DNS rebinding, CWE-352) from the advisory's bind-address fix; the server is documented as dev-only/local, so a solver can argue browser attacks are out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fallback fix site (src/server.rs), ~80 lines below start()

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Workspace-mode serve path could plausibly construct its own listener / fallback address instead of calling crate::server::start.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Workspace mode already builds its own ServerContext separately (src/workspace.rs:698-704, 713-719); a maintainer adding workspace-specific serving would naturally copy the bind/fallback logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Live-reload WebSocket served on a separate listener with its own default bind (e.g. 0.0.0.0:35729).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Many live-reload tools use a dedicated port; here it shares the HTTP listener (src/server.rs:156-160), so a split-out listener is a realistic refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A marmite.yaml `serve_bind`/`server.host` config key merged under CLI args with a 0.0.0.0 default.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Config already carries serve-related settings (enable_toolbar) and CLI-overrides-config merging exists (site_data.site.override_from_cli_args, src/main.rs:295).

O9_family: missing authentication / unintended network exposure of dev-server write API (CWE-306, insecure default bind)

O10_build.project_tests: src/tests/server.rs (10 tests at pinned commit, none on binding); CLI parse tests possible via crate::cli::Cli::try_parse_from as the fix does

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change the clap default in src/cli.rs:60 to 127.0.0.1:8000 and leave the 0.0.0.0:0 fallback in src/server.rs:26/104 untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: handle_file_api path check is a substring '..' filter on the raw relative path (src/server.rs:881-884); path-traversal class, not this advisory.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell used); tiny_repo flag not assessed.

O8 Host/Origin route is a different mechanism from the published bind fix; counting it as the advisory's property (unauthenticated API access) is a judgement call and hidden tests for it would need the report to describe browser-origin access.
Whether tiny_http 0.12 Server::http(&str) at src/server.rs:98 binds all resolved addresses or only the first for hostnames was not checked.
